### Module 04 — Machine Learning for Clinical Prediction

# ML Pipeline Setup & Train/Test Splits

***
**Learning objectives**
- Understand why random splits fail in clinical settings and when temporal splits are required
- Build a reproducible preprocessing pipeline with `recipes` / `workflows`
- Handle class imbalance with SMOTE, class weights, and under-sampling
- Apply stratified k-fold and time-series cross-validation correctly
- Establish a baseline model (majority classifier, logistic regression) to beat

**Estimated time:** 2 hours | **Level:** Intermediate | **Libraries:** `dplyr`, `tibble`, `tidymodels`, `ggplot2`

## 1. Setup & Dataset


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(patchwork)
tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(42)

mod04_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod04")
dir.create(mod04_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

col_blue   <- "#2563EB"
col_red    <- "#DC2626"
col_green  <- "#16A34A"
col_navy   <- "#1E3A8A"

auc_prob   <- function(y, p) yardstick::roc_auc_vec(factor(y, levels = c(0, 1)), p, event_level = "second")
ap_prob    <- function(y, p) yardstick::pr_auc_vec(factor(y, levels = c(0, 1)), p, event_level = "second")
brier_prob <- function(y, p) mean((p - as.numeric(as.character(y)))^2)

# ── Reconstruct shared dataset ────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 3000
sig <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
clip <- function(x, lo, hi) pmin(pmax(x, lo), hi)
b <- matrix(rnorm(N * 4), ncol = 4)
set.seed(99)
age          <- as.integer(clip(rnorm(N, 62, 15), 18, 92))
sex          <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payer        <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                       N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
admit_type   <- sample(c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent"),
                       N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.18))
los_days     <- as.integer(clip(round(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8)), 1, 30))
diabetes     <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(0.6 * b[, 1] - 0.5 + 0.02 * (age - 62) / 15))
hypertension <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(0.7 * b[, 1] - 0.2))
hf           <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(0.4 * b[, 2] + 0.5 * hypertension - 1.5))
copd         <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(0.5 * b[, 3] - 1.0))
ckd          <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(0.5 * b[, 1] + 0.6 * diabetes - 1.2))
obesity      <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(0.5 * b[, 1] - 0.8))
depression   <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(0.3 * b[, 4] - 1.4))
n_comorb     <- diabetes + hypertension + hf + copd + ckd
set.seed(21)
glucose      <- round(clip(rnorm(N, 105 + 15 * diabetes, 28), 50, 400), 1)
creatinine   <- round(clip(rgamma(N, shape = 1.6 + 0.8 * hf, scale = 0.6), 0.4, 10), 2)
hba1c        <- round(clip(rnorm(N, 6.5 + 0.8 * diabetes, 1.4), 4, 14), 1)
sbp          <- round(clip(rnorm(N, 128 + 12 * hypertension, 18), 80, 200), 0)
bmi          <- round(clip(rnorm(N, 28 + 4 * obesity, 6), 15, 55), 1)
logit <- (-3.2 + 0.6 * hf + 0.5 * diabetes + 0.5 * ckd + 0.3 * copd +
            0.02 * (age - 62) / 15 +
            0.3 * as.integer(admit_type == "Emergency") +
            0.25 * as.integer(payer == "Medicaid") +
            0.2 * as.integer(los_days > 7) +
            0.5 * hf * diabetes + rnorm(N, 0, 0.25))
readmitted <- rbinom(N, 1, sig(logit))
# Add admission dates for temporal split demonstration
start <- as.Date("2019-01-01")
set.seed(5)
admit_dates <- start + sample.int(as.integer(as.Date("2023-12-31") - start), N, replace = TRUE)

df <- tibble(
  patient_id   = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age, sex, payer, admit_type, los_days,
  diabetes, hypertension, hf, copd,
  ckd, obesity, depression, n_comorb,
  glucose, creatinine, hba1c, sbp, bmi,
  readmitted, admit_date = admit_dates
) %>%
  arrange(admit_date)
df$los_gt7 <- as.integer(df$los_days > 7)
NUMERIC   <- c("age", "los_days", "n_comorb", "glucose", "creatinine", "hba1c", "sbp", "bmi")
BINARY    <- c("diabetes", "hypertension", "hf", "copd", "ckd", "obesity", "depression", "los_gt7")
CATEGORIC <- c("sex", "payer", "admit_type")
FEATURES  <- c(NUMERIC, BINARY, CATEGORIC)
TARGET    <- "readmitted"
cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d x %d | Positive rate: %.1f%%\n",
            nrow(df), ncol(df), mean(df[[TARGET]]) * 100))
```

## 2. Why Temporal Splits Matter in Healthcare

Random splitting of clinical data **leaks future information into training** when:
- The same patient appears multiple times (train on visit 1, test on visit 2 of the *same patient*)
- Care patterns change over time (COVID, policy changes, new guidelines)
- Models evaluated on temporal holdouts reflect real-world deployment performance

| Split type | Use when | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| Random stratified | Cross-sectional data, no time structure | Data leakage if temporal trends exist |
| Temporal (chronological) | Time-ordered admissions, EHR data | Better reflects deployment conditions |
| Patient-level | Same patient across visits | Prevents same-patient leakage |
| Geographic | Multi-site data | Tests transportability |


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# ── Temporal split: train 2019-2021, validate 2022, test 2023 ─────────────────
df <- df %>% mutate(admit_year = as.integer(format(admit_date, "%Y")))
df_train <- df %>% filter(admit_year <= 2021)
df_val   <- df %>% filter(admit_year == 2022)
df_test  <- df %>% filter(admit_year == 2023)
```

## 3. Preprocessing Pipeline


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# recipes / workflows ensure: (1) no data leakage (prep on train, bake test)
#                             (2) reproducible, deployable preprocessing

train_ml <- df_train %>%
  select(all_of(c(FEATURES, TARGET))) %>%
  mutate(readmitted = factor(readmitted, levels = c(0, 1)))
val_ml <- df_val %>%
  select(all_of(c(FEATURES, TARGET))) %>%
  mutate(readmitted = factor(readmitted, levels = c(0, 1)))
test_ml <- df_test %>%
  select(all_of(c(FEATURES, TARGET))) %>%
  mutate(readmitted = factor(readmitted, levels = c(0, 1)))

rec <- recipe(readmitted ~ ., data = train_ml) %>%
  step_impute_median(all_of(NUMERIC)) %>%
  step_normalize(all_of(NUMERIC)) %>%
  step_impute_median(all_of(BINARY)) %>%
  step_impute_mode(all_of(CATEGORIC)) %>%
  step_dummy(all_of(CATEGORIC), one_hot = TRUE)

# Fit on train, transform val and test
rec_prep   <- prep(rec, training = train_ml)
X_train_pp <- as.matrix(bake(rec_prep, new_data = train_ml) %>% select(-readmitted))
X_val_pp   <- as.matrix(bake(rec_prep, new_data = val_ml)   %>% select(-readmitted))
X_test_pp  <- as.matrix(bake(rec_prep, new_data = test_ml)  %>% select(-readmitted))
y_train    <- df_train[[TARGET]]
y_val      <- df_val[[TARGET]]
y_test     <- df_test[[TARGET]]

cat("Preprocessed shapes:\n")
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# Strategy comparison — SMOTE-style interpolation, under-sampling, SMOTE+Tomek
smote_resample <- function(x, y, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  pos <- which(y == 1); neg <- which(y == 0)
  n_need <- length(neg) - length(pos)
  if (n_need <= 0) return(list(x = x, y = y))
  xp <- x[pos, , drop = FALSE]
  i1 <- sample(nrow(xp), n_need, replace = TRUE)
  i2 <- sample(nrow(xp), n_need, replace = TRUE)
  lam <- runif(n_need)
  syn <- xp[i1, , drop = FALSE] * lam + xp[i2, , drop = FALSE] * (1 - lam)
  list(x = rbind(x, syn), y = c(y, rep(1L, n_need)))
}
under_resample <- function(x, y, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  pos <- which(y == 1); neg <- which(y == 0)
  n <- min(length(pos), length(neg))
  idx <- c(sample(pos, n), sample(neg, n))
  list(x = x[idx, , drop = FALSE], y = y[idx])
}
tomek_clean <- function(x, y) {
  # Drop majority points whose nearest neighbour is minority (Tomek-style)
  d <- as.matrix(dist(x))
  diag(d) <- Inf
  nn <- apply(d, 1, which.min)
  drop <- which(y == 0 & y[nn] == 1)
  keep <- setdiff(seq_along(y), drop)
  list(x = x[keep, , drop = FALSE], y = y[keep])
}

strategies <- list(Original = list(x = X_train_pp, y = y_train))
sm  <- smote_resample(X_train_pp, y_train, seed = 42)
rus <- under_resample(X_train_pp, y_train, seed = 42)
smt <- tomek_clean(sm$x, sm$y)
strategies[["SMOTE"]]        <- sm
strategies[["Under-sample"]] <- rus
strategies[["SMOTE+Tomek"]]  <- smt

counts <- imap_dfr(strategies, function(xy, name) {
  tibble(strategy = name,
         Negative = sum(xy$y == 0),
         Positive = sum(xy$y == 1))
}) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Negative, Positive), names_to = "cls", values_to = "n")

ggplot(counts, aes(strategy, n, fill = cls)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.65, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Negative" = col_blue, "Positive" = col_red)) +
  labs(y = "N samples", x = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Class distribution by resampling strategy")
```

## 5. Baseline Models — the Bar to Beat


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Every ML project needs baselines. If your fancy model can't beat these, something is wrong.
set.seed(42)
train_df <- as_tibble(X_train_pp) %>% mutate(y = y_train)
val_df   <- as_tibble(X_val_pp)

# Majority class (always predict 0) — P(y=1) = 0
prob_maj <- rep(0, length(y_val))

# Random (stratified) — one-hot draws from the training class distribution
p_pos <- mean(y_train)
prob_strat <- as.numeric(rbinom(length(y_val), 1, p_pos))

# Logistic Regression (L2) with balanced class weights via glm
w_bal <- ifelse(y_train == 1, 0.5 / mean(y_train == 1), 0.5 / mean(y_train == 0))
lr_fit <- glm(y ~ ., data = train_df, family = binomial, weights = w_bal)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
         `Avg Precision` = round(ap, 4), Brier = round(brier, 4))
})
```

## 6. Cross-Validation Strategies


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Compare stratified k-fold vs time-series CV on the training set
cv_auc_fold <- function(x, y, tr_idx, te_idx) {
  dtr <- as_tibble(x[tr_idx, , drop = FALSE]) %>% mutate(y = y[tr_idx])
  dte <- as_tibble(x[te_idx, , drop = FALSE])
  w   <- ifelse(y[tr_idx] == 1, 0.5 / mean(y[tr_idx] == 1),
                0.5 / mean(y[tr_idx] == 0))
  fit <- glm(y ~ ., data = dtr, family = binomial, weights = w)
  auc_prob(y[te_idx], predict(fit, newdata = dte, type = "response"))
}

# Stratified k-fold (appropriate for cross-sectional data)
set.seed(42)
train_cv <- as_tibble(X_train_pp) %>% mutate(y = factor(y_train, levels = c(0, 1)))
skf <- vfold_cv(train_cv, v = 5, strata = y)
cv_skf <- map_dbl(skf$splits, function(sp) {
  cv_auc_fold(X_train_pp, y_train, as.integer(sp$in_id),
              setdiff(seq_len(nrow(train_cv)), as.integer(sp$in_id)))
})
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# Time-series split (for temporal data — each fold extends the train window)
# Expanding-window analogue of tidymodels rolling_origin / TimeSeriesSplit
n <- nrow(X_train_pp)
n_splits <- 5
n_test <- floor(n / (n_splits + 1))
cv_tss <- map_dbl(seq_len(n_splits), function(i) {
  train_end <- i * n_test + (n %% (n_splits + 1))
  test_end  <- train_end + n_test
  tr_idx <- seq_len(train_end)
  te_idx <- (train_end + 1):min(test_end, n)
  cv_auc_fold(X_train_pp, y_train, tr_idx, te_idx)
})
```

## 7. Knowledge Check
1. You have 5 years of EHR data. A colleague proposes random 80/20 split. What are the risks, and what would you recommend instead?
2. Your positive class rate is 13%. What class-weight setting should you pass to tidymodels / ranger models?
3. SMOTE creates synthetic samples. What is the risk of applying SMOTE *before* splitting into train/test?
4. Logistic regression baseline AUC = 0.74. Your XGBoost gets 0.75. Is this improvement clinically meaningful?
5. Implement patient-level split: ensure no patient appears in both train and test.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Exercise 5 — patient-level split (each PT only in one split)
# In real datasets, use MRN/patient_id grouping
set.seed(42)
groups <- as.integer(sub("PT-", "", df$patient_id)) %% 100  # simulate patient groups
group_ids <- sort(unique(groups))
n_te_g <- floor(0.20 * length(group_ids))
test_groups  <- sample(group_ids, n_te_g)
train_groups <- setdiff(group_ids, test_groups)
tr_idx <- which(groups %in% train_groups)
te_idx <- which(groups %in% test_groups)
cat(sprintf("Patient-level split: train N=%d, test N=%d\n", length(tr_idx), length(te_idx)))
```
